candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 78-year-old man and U.S. citizen living in Idaho. He identifies as White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category that includes people of European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries. He is married to June; they have no children. Their gross household income is about $228,000 a year, mainly from pensions and retirement investments, though they still plan around taxes, medical costs, and home upkeep. He is moderately conservative, valuing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while accepting public programs such as Medicare. He reads for pleasure, especially river memoirs, wildlife writing, and practical books about watersheds.
candidates.life_course: He retired after a career as a civil engineer working on water and irrigation projects. His work left him attentive to how a river behaves, but fishing became a separate pleasure rather than another technical assignment. June enjoys being outdoors but does not fish, and they have made a comfortable life together without children.
candidates.daily_life: He ties flies at a workbench, checks local river conditions, and fishes with two longtime friends when schedules and weather line up. He also spends occasional mornings helping with a local stream-monitoring effort. June joins him for walks and some riverside outings; at home they read in the evenings and share ordinary household decisions.
candidates.travel: He travels to fish unfamiliar rivers and to understand what makes each stretch of water different: its current, banks, fish habitat, and the ways nearby residents care for it. On a past trip to western Montana, he chose to spend a morning at a volunteer stream-restoration workday before taking his rod out; he still tells the story because the work changed what he noticed while fishing. He usually travels with June and sometimes coordinates a few days with his fishing friends. They drive, bring his own gear, and book a cabin or modest lodge near the river, with a comfortable place for June to read while he is out. He prefers a few unhurried days on one river to packing several stops into a trip.
candidates.personality_and_voice: He is patient with water and weather, less patient with vague claims about conservation. In conversation he tends to ask practical questions, then listen closely to the answer. His humor is dry, and he would rather show someone how to tie a knot than give a long speech about it.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 82-year-old American man residing in Colorado. He identifies as White, non-Hispanic, in the broad census-style category encompassing European, Middle Eastern, North African, and other ancestries. He is married to Ruth, and they have no children. Their gross household income is approximately $246,000 annually, from retirement income, investments, and Ruth’s pension; they are comfortable but attentive to health expenses and financial planning. He is moderately conservative, emphasizing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while supporting some public programs. He enjoys reading for pleasure, particularly cookbooks, food memoirs, and books about regional traditions.
candidates.life_course: He spent most of his career in food-service distribution, first visiting kitchens and later managing a regional sales team. Those years introduced him to cooks with very different habits; after retirement, he began cooking seriously at home. Ruth likes good food but is happy to leave the stove to him.
candidates.daily_life: He plans a meal around what looks good at the market, then cooks with Ruth nearby or invites two familiar couples to eat. He revises recipes in a notebook and reads cookbooks as much for their stories as their instructions. He enjoys being the host, though he can get particular about timing and seasoning.
candidates.travel: He wants to taste how a place’s ingredients, migration, and everyday customs shape what people cook, not simply collect famous restaurants. On a previous trip to coastal Maine, he and Ruth tried several versions of chowder and talked with a café owner about how family recipes had changed over time; that conversation mattered to him as much as the meals. Future trips appeal when they offer local dishes, a market visit, or an informal cooking session with someone who knows the food firsthand. They usually travel together, drive or fly depending on distance, and choose a comfortable inn or hotel as a base. Philip likes leaving enough open time to follow a recommendation rather than scheduling every meal in advance.
candidates.personality_and_voice: He is hospitable and sociable, but takes charge when a meal is underway. He will praise a dish generously, then bluntly explain what he would change. He enjoys asking people about their cooking and is at his most animated when comparing two versions of the same recipe.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 76-year-old male U.S. citizen who lives in Montana. He identifies as White, non-Hispanic, using the broad census-style category that includes European, Middle Eastern, North African, and other ancestries. He is married to Miriam; they have no children. Their gross household income is around $258,000 per year, supported by retirement income and investments, with some continuing costs from maintaining their home. He is moderately conservative, valuing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while recognizing a role for public programs. He reads for enjoyment, especially biographies, architectural histories, and accounts of changing American towns.
candidates.life_course: A retired architect, he spent decades designing civic and commercial buildings. In retirement, his interest shifted from producing plans to noticing how older buildings were altered, reused, or allowed to disappear. Miriam, a retired nurse, likes the walks and the stories but is less interested in debating construction details.
candidates.daily_life: He volunteers with a local historical group, helping document older buildings and occasionally recording residents’ recollections. He reads in the morning, then walks downtown with Miriam or makes notes from photographs and old maps. He likes having a specific question to investigate, such as why a building’s entrance or windows changed.
candidates.travel: He travels to see how communities have lived with their built history: old main streets, depots, industrial buildings, and civic spaces that have found a second use. On a past trip to an older mill town, he chose a walking tour and ended up talking at length with a local preservation volunteer about which parts of a building were original. That exchange made the visit memorable because it connected architecture to local choices and livelihoods. He usually travels with Miriam, taking a camera and notebook and arranging a few days around one town rather than a rapid circuit. They drive when practical and stay near the area they plan to explore. He leaves time for conversation and for Miriam to choose some stops of her own.
candidates.personality_and_voice: He is precise, opinionated, and fond of a good disagreement. He may interrupt to distinguish an original feature from a later addition, but he is willing to change his mind when someone brings better evidence. In a group he asks pointed questions rather than making small talk.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 86-year-old man, an American citizen living in Colorado. He identifies as White, non-Hispanic, in the broad census-style category that includes European, Middle Eastern, North African, and other ancestries. He is married to Eleanor, and they have no children. Their gross annual household income is about $216,000, mostly from pensions and retirement investments; they are financially secure but mindful of health and home-maintenance costs. He is moderately conservative, emphasizing personal responsibility, tradition, and limits on government while accepting public programs. He enjoys reading for leisure, especially astronomy and science books, along with biographies.
candidates.life_course: He retired from a career in radio and communications engineering. A neighbor introduced him to amateur astronomy later in life, and he gradually acquired a telescope and learned to keep careful observing notes. Eleanor is not as absorbed in equipment, but she enjoys joining him for especially striking sky events.
candidates.daily_life: He maintains his telescope, records observations, and meets a small astronomy-club group to compare what they have seen. He enjoys helping a newcomer get a first clear view through the eyepiece, then prefers to return to quiet observation. At home he reads, follows his notes, and discusses plans with Eleanor.
candidates.travel: He travels for dark skies and for the chance to observe a particular celestial event with other enthusiasts. A past trip planned around a total eclipse remains vivid to him: he remembers the change in the light and the hushed reaction of the people watching alongside him. He also likes trips where he can spend several nights comparing observations rather than treating the sky as a brief spectacle. He and Eleanor usually travel together; for longer journeys they plan daylight driving, bring the telescope securely packed, and look for lodging with a suitable place to set it up. He checks the forecast and coordinates with club friends, while accepting that clouds can defeat even careful plans.
candidates.personality_and_voice: He is reserved in a crowd and more expressive when explaining what he has observed. His humor is understated, and he can be stubborn about recording things accurately. He is welcoming to curious beginners, but has little appetite for loud socializing that competes with a clear night.
